Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8193311
Permit API: 059-24246
Unconventional: No
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/02/2024
Comments: On 07/02/24 an incident inspection of the Walker 1 Well Site was conducted in response to the report of a spill received by the Department on 07/02/24. (CTS: 381922). Background:On 07/02/24 Greylock self-reported a brine release at the Walker 1 well. On 07/02/24 I spoke to Trevor Woods of Greylock to acquire additional details about the spill. During the inspection it was determined that an estimated 60 barrels of produced water had been released to the well area from a crack at the bottom of the poly tank being used on site. Investigation showed that the release was contained to the well area and no water ways were impacted. Remediation efforts were underway at the time of my inspection. Findings:-A well tag was observed on the well head (Photo #1).-The spill is suspected to have originated from a crack at the bottom of the tank (Photos #2-3).-Elevated conductivity was observed in the substrate in the spill area (Photos #4-9). -Crews were present on-site working to remediate the spill. (Photo #10). -No elevated conductivity was observed outside of the spill area.No discharge to surface water was observed. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78.54 are being issued for the release of brine to the ground.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/25/2025 to KRIEBEL NATURAL GAS CO LLC in East Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: KRIEBEL NATURAL GAS CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/25/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8226729
Permit API: 129-26623
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: East Huntingdon Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2025
Comments: On March 25, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection of the Wissinger 001 Well in regards to an incident reported to the Department at 10:25 am of an explosion at the well site. Present during the inspection were several representatives from Kriebel including Shane Kriebel, Jay Niehenke, Ronald Seich, Josh Hosteler, Nello Fossi, Ben Dicken, and Charles Reaggle (DEP).-This is inspection 1 of a 2 part inspection-Upon arriving onsite the Department spoke to Shane Kriebel. Mr. Kriebel stated that an explosion of the production tank had occurred while the well tender was blowing out the well, at approximately 9:40 am. Mr. Kriebel stated they believe the explosion was caused by a faulty or damaged grounding wire. He stated that approximately 10 barrels of an oil and brine mixture was released. He stated that remediation was underway and that they would be following Act 2 for this clean up. He stated that saw dust and roughly 4 bags of Oil Gator were used to soak up any standing and pooled brine/oil in order to prevent further leaching in to the ground and easier excavation. He stated they had installed booms in the ditch behind the well site to prevent further migration of the released oil and brine.The Department's observations are as follows:At the time of the Department's arrival, the Department observed an area roughly 40 feet around the production equipment that appeared heavily saturated with an orange tinted fluid, presumably an oil and brine mixture. The Department observed what appeared to be the bottom portion of the production tank on the ground near the rest of the production equipment. A light-colored powder(Oil Gator) was observed placed on the ground in the area where the production tank previously was. A ditch that extended along the western perimeter of the well site, and down slope near the southern perimeter was observed. There appeared to be released fluid in this ditch directly behind the production equipment area, as well as in the ditch downslope on the southern perimeter totaling roughly 120 feet of ditch that appeared to be impacted. 2 booms and hay bales were observed installed in the ditch, one approximately 25 feet north of the production equipment, and one approximately 70 feet downslope south of the production equipment.The Department then began to obtain conductivity readings in the area surrounding the production equipment as well as in the ditch. Conductivity readings in the area surrounding the production equipment were OR (over of detectable range, over 20mS), in approximately a 25 foot radius in which readings then appeared to be comparable to background readings of 0.16mS. Conductivity readings in the ditch were also OR, however readings appear to become comparable to the background reading near the northern boom installed with a reading taken at the boom of 0.19mS. Readings at the southern boom installed were OR, with readings taken approximately 15 feet downslope of the southern boom of 13.23mS. The Department recommended to Mr.Kriebel that additional measures be taken to prevent the migration of contaminates downslope. Mr. Kriebel then had an additional boom installed downslope of the previously installed one on the southern perimeter.

Violation Code: 105.46(a) - IMPLEMENTATION OF EROSION AND SEDIMENTATION CONTROL PLANS – During construction of water obstruction or encroachment, permittee failed to follow the erosion and sediment control plan prepared in accordance with Chapter 102 (relating to erosion and sediment control) and submitted as part of the application.
Violation ID: 8275344
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/14/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted to evaluate the status of violations issued on 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 associated with the construction of the well site for this proposed conventional well and the access road leading to it. Since the 4/17/2026 inspection, Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) submitted multiple versions of an updated E and S plan that included additional BMPs and methods to stabilize all disturbed areas. At the time of this inspection, the latest version of the updated E and S plan has not yet met the expectations of the Department's Technical Services staff, as was indicated in a 5/11/2026 email to William Cenk.Throughout this inspection, we observed that a majority of the practices prescribed in the latest version of the updated E and S plan have been implemented. Inlet/outlet rock protection was placed at the installed culverts, rock filters placed in the roadside ditch in the vicinity of the well site for proposed Well # 3, and a combination of erosion blankets and mulch was applied to temporarily stabilize most of the disturbed areas. TMP indicated that seed was applied prior to mulching/placement of the erosion blanket. Erosion blanket was missing upslope of Culvert 1 and there was no evidence of hydro-seeding. The placement of grubbing material along the southern side of the access road that has displaced stream flow continues to result in accelerated erosion and washout along the southern edge of the road and perimeter of the well site for proposed Well # 4.The Department suggests the removal of the stockpile material from approximately the outlet location of Culvert 3 westerly to the newly established point of concentrated flow. Currently, it appears the streamflow is obstructed and migrated towards the pad/access road creating concentrated flow which cannot be stabilized. Without proper stabilization, the additional flow due to the construction activity appears to be causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation to Wetland G. The removal of the waste areas would potentially allow the flow to migrate back to its original drainage path and allow for successful installation of temporary stabilization BMPs, per plan. Department staff can be available for consultation/direction during the removal operation. Waste areas are not to be discarded in other floodways or wetlands. After the submission of the updated and complete E and S plan to Brian Ayers (brayers@pa.gov), temporary stabilization shall be finished. A follow up inspection will be conducted following the completion of the temporary stabilization. A preapplication meeting must be submitted/scheduled before June 15, 2026 in order to address any outstanding violations.Violations that were cited in the 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 inspection reports remain unaddressed.The following were in attendance for this inspection:DEP - Aquatic Biologist Samantha Lutz, Aquatic Biologist Jessica McDuff and WQSS Brian Ayers.Trinity Mineral Partners - Kyle Miller, Brian Bennett and Todd Fantaskey (Northwest Soil Services)

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
Violation ID: 836269
Permit API: 059-27587
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Richhill Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2018-12-07
Comments: On December 7, 2018, the Department performed an inspection of the CNX RHL22 well pad site. The site is located in Richhill Twp., Greene County. The inspection was a follow up inspection related to a reported reuse water release to the well pad on 12/1/18, and violations issued on 12/3/18. The operator initially reported a 30 barrel reuse water release to the well pad @ 01:15 a.m. on 12/1/18. The operator did contact the Department at 11:00 a.m. on 12/1/18 to report that the release was greater and was approximately 210 barrels of reuse water. The operator has reported that during the transfer of reuse water from the constructed MASS on the tank pad, along the access road, to the working tanks a communication error occurred and the working tanks were over filled causing a release of approximately 210 barrels of reuse water to the well pad. The reuse water overwhelmed the well pad secondary containment discharging to the well pad and storm water collection channels for the site. The reuse water then entered the PCSM structure discharging off site. The collection channel to the PCSM was also overwhelmed and the water was discharged onto the RHL28 gathering pipeline ROW adjacent to the well pad site. The operator was excavating impacted material off site on the pipeline ROW at time of inspection. The operator was also excavating the PCSM and PCSM collection channel at time of inspection. The operator was using field conductivity readings to direct the excavation activities. The operator had attempted to plug the PCSM discharge structure, with an inflatable rubber plug, but was unable to do so. The Department observed elevated conductivity readings in the standing water and soils on the southwest corner of the well pad, as well as the storm water controls for this area. Elevated conductivity readings were also observed off the well pad site on the pipeline ROW and down gradient from both sites during the 12/3/18 inspection. The operator has completed hydraulic fracturing operations on the site and has begun removing the equipment necessary for hydraulic fracturing from the well pad. The operator has reported to the Department that secondary containment will be setup on the well pad to store excavated, impacted soils for disposal and remediation efforts will continue all weekend and into next week on the well pad as well as in the PCSM structures impacted by the reuse water spill.

Comments: On 10/31/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 43 degrees, overcast and lightly sprinkling when I arrived on location. Rainfall has impacted the region in the last 24 hours.Upon my arrival, I first inspected the original south pad for the Taft 851 1V well. A plugged well monument is installed above the well with a plugged date of 3/24/2025. All servicing equipment has been removed from this pad. The pad has not been reclaimed and the temporary access road and temporary bridges remain installed.When I arrive on the active site, I met Seneca's Wes Sammins who described current operations as follows: Patterson drilling rig #805 has been mobilized to the site to drill an additional eight wells at the site. The rig was towered up over the 70HU, and had started drilling surface on 10/28/2025. The rig was currently drilling the intermediate at 1568 feet with the intermediate going to 3350 feet, then to total depth at 23514 feet. Wes expects to drill one more well that is in the process of being repermitted. Six wells have been completed this run. Secondary containment has been installed for drilling operations. 12 frac tanks, diesel tanks, and chemicals were staged in secondary containment around the drilling rig. Drill cuttings were being collected, solidified and temporarily stored in 6 dumpsters. 28 frac tanks remain staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. There are five newly drilled and completed wells on site that were staged for production. Sand separators were attached to the wells, the sand separators all connected to two frac tanks. Secondary containment remains installed around the wellheads. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs have been installed on site, all staged in secondary containment. Liquid in a 5' x 40' puddle on the unprotected ground north of the GPUs field tested at 1875 mS conductance. I discussed this with Wes who arranged for the liquid to be removed.A 40 foot channel of water immediately east of the central outfall from the pad field tested at 2030 uS conductance. Liquid draining from the north center outfall into the basin field tested at 2020 uS conductance. Liquid in the sediment basin next to the northeast overflow field tested at 1380 uS conductance. Liquid was observed flowing through the northern most compost filter sock and leaving the site; the liquid field tested at 1201 uS conductance. Liquid flowing past the LOD field tested at 1409 uS conductance.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1200 hours.

Comments On 3/7/17, Mr. Kepler with Seneca Resources contacted the Department regarding a small release of production fluid from a booster pump near the intersection of Middle Fork Road and Shawmut Grade Road. The pump is installed along a temporary water line running from Seneca's F10-F pad to their Clermont Storage Facility. The following was submitted to the Department in an email from Mr. Kepler: "The attached photo depicts the cracked head of a booster pump that was being used to move fluid from the F10-F flowback to the storage facility. An operator was on location when the incident occurred and the unit was immediately shut down and the isolation valves were closed. There were no injuries. A minimal amount of fluid was released as a spray, but the roadside ditch water associated with today's rain storms was impacted." The release was estimated to have lasted 15 seconds, releasing approximately 15-20 gallons of production fluid from Seneca's 047-24926 and 047 -24927 wells, both producing fluid at the time of the release. Upon inspection, soil conductivity readings were below 200 uS/cm along the ditch. The fluid released to the ditch had also been removed. The release constitutes violations of CSL 307(a), SWMA 301, and 78a57(a). These violations are being cited for both active wells that were producing fluid during the release. All violations will be resolved, as they were immediately corrected. Failed to properly store/transport production fluid.

Comments: The DEP completed an administrative inspection on Blackhill Energy's Kinglsey E 7H well(API 015-23676) located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 12/7/2021. The inspection was completed in order to summarize sample results from a sample collected during the 11/10/2021 inspection (IR #3282018). On 11/10/2021, I inspected Blackhill Energy's Kingsley E well site and discovered elevated electrical conductivity puddles off of the pad-wide containment. Elevated electrical conductivity puddles were field measured utilizing an Oakton PCSTestr 35 and ranged in field readings from 5.4 to 9.0 mS/cm. A sample for standard analysis code 942 was collected on 11/10/2021 from a puddle field measured at ~7.7mS/cm (0983-254). The sample was later received by the DEP Laboratory in Harrisburg, PA on 11/16/2021 and the final sample results were reported on 12/4/2021. The DEP's analytical sample results are attached as photos and as a file. Additional information regarding the initial inspection can be found in inspection record #3282018. The operator responded immediately after notification of the discovery. The operator believed the containment berms were driven over and crushed, which allowed the elevated electrical conductivity water that was on containment to be spilled off of containment. The operator estimated the back (northeastern) side to be less than 1 gallon while the front (southwestern) side was reported to be less than 4 gallons, but was then mixed with freshwater which was sprayed on the pad for dust control. The operator explained that they planned on remediating the impacted area and placing rig mats in front of the driving areas, so trucks will drive over the rig mats and not over the containment berms. At around 1500 hours the next day, 11/11/2021, the operator provided me photos of the remediation (see photos #3 & 4). Based on the findings of inspection record #3282018 and sample results 0983-254 violations of the following are cited against API # 015-23676: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 35 P.S. 6018.301 Due to the timely response of remediation efforts completed by the operator, these violations will be cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED and will be closed at this time.

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/25/2024
Comments: This conventional well is equipped for production with a pump jack. A sign containing the API number, well name, and operator information was posted on a stake near the well. The GPS coordinate on file for this well was verified as part of this inspection. Upon arrival to the site, it was evident that crude oil had recently leaked from a faulty stuffing box on this well. The discharged crude oil migrated onto the well site, then traveled linearly approximately 450 feet downslope of the well on the access road. The crude oil remained contained on the road surface and ultimately accumulated in a puddle of standing water at the bottom of the hill (see Photo 2). It is estimated that less than 1 barrel of crude oil has been released as part of this incident. No waterways have been affected from the event.A representative from Bull Run Resources, JR McLaughlin, was contacted in response to the event. He arrived to the site immediately to address the noted concerns. The leaking stuffing box was repaired and diapers were used to absorb the crude oil from the road surface and around the well head. Given there is no ongoing discharge and a bulk of the released product has been remediated, the violations associated with this incident are considered corrected.A future inspection will be conducted to ensure that the initial remediation efforts were sufficient.

Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to inspection 2995415 conducted on 2/10/2020 in which sediment laden storm water was observed leaving the operators access road and entering a stream. Only the portion of the access road where the discharge was occurring is being inspected. PADEP Eric Norman is assisting and Operator representative Isaac Haky is on site. The access road appears to have been regraded and CFS put down on the road side ditch side of the access road. While the regrading has abated the accelerated erosion rills observed in previous inspections, the Department recommends that the operator stabilize the access road to prevent a reoccurrence. The operator appears to have laid down stone on the portion of the access road which was previously pooling water and no pooled water or discharges are observed at this time. Based on this observation the CSL violations will be closed as corrected/abated effective 3/2/2020. The operator has placed CFS on the road side ditch side of the access road, the CFS is not installed per the E&S Manual. The Department recommends that the operator install CFS per the E&S Manual detail 4-1. It appears that the rock laid at this location does not adequately cover the entire width of the access road leaving a strip on either side bare. The Department recommends that the operator stabilize these “shoulders” to prevent the possibility of accelerated erosion from occurring. Based on this inspection the CSL violations will be closed as corrected/abated. No new violations will be issued for this inspection. A follow up inspection for the other outstanding violations will be scheduled for a later date.

Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEP's Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. Violations for failure to plug upon abandonment are continuing as of this inspection.

Comments: On 1/7/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine inspection at the Seneca Vandergrift 290 well site located in Charleston Twp, Tioga Co. It was 40 degrees and overcast when I arrived on site. Snow and ice from recent snowfall events still covered the facility.During the inspection, Moody and associates had a team on site collecting samples from the three clean-out standpipes from the monitoring trenches draining from the well cellars. A conductivity reading from the east clean-out pipe was 1.14 mS conductance. There are four active wells on site staged for production, along with one plugged well and one that is in the process of being plugged. The Vandergrift 290 2H well has a monument with plugged date of 12/4/2024. The 5H well still has the production valve attached. The production tanks and GPUs are staged in secondary containment.Temporary compost filter socks remain installed below the excavated/remediated areas. Ice and snow cover the restored area. Temporary stabilization could be seen in areas not covered by snow. PCSM structures have not been installed at this location.Violations are still outstanding for inspection IDs 3999274 and 4029808 for a release of an unknown amount of produced water to the unprotected pad surface, to the unprotected grassy field below the fill slope and flowing offsite during plugging operations.The DEP recommends the following:1. Continue monitoring the area for contamination.2. Continue remediation efforts as necessary. 3. Continue collecting fluids that demonstrate elevated conductance.I left the site at 1400 hours.
